technical_and_design_decisions: U1 (Transaction Context): For Node.js, the context object (stub, etc.) is naturally the first parameter. For Java, to ensure thread-safety, a new transaction context object will be instantiated and scoped to each chaincode invocation, which is the recommended pattern in Hyperledger Fabric Java Chaincode.

U2/U3 (Package Cleanup): The refactoring will involve physically moving the 'protos/utils' directory to a new 'protoutils' package location. This requires updating all internal imports and any documented public API paths. The approach will be a careful rename-and-update to avoid breaking the core.

U4 (Kafka Health Checks): This feature is specified as being already on the 'master' branch. The primary technical task is to backport/merge the existing, tested commit(s) into the specified release (1.4 LTS) branch, ensuring compatibility and running regression tests.

U5 (Reader Invoke for Query): The design decision is to implement access control based on the actual chaincode operations performed. A new `InvokeChaincode` policy will be introduced that evaluates the set of operations (e.g., `GetState`, `PutState`) in the transaction proposal. A `chaincode` performing only read (`Get`) operations will be allowed with Reader permission. This requires changes to the core transaction validation logic.

U6 (Service Discovery Endpoint): A new peer configuration option, e.g., `CORE_PEER_SERVICE_DISCOVERY_EXTERNAL_ENDPOINT`, will be added. If set, this value will be used in Service Discovery advertisements instead of the gossip external endpoint. This provides a clean separation for development environments.

U7 (Operations Service Version): A new REST endpoint, e.g., `/version`, will be added to the existing operations service (which typically uses HTTP/gRPC on a separate port). The endpoint will return the peer or orderer's build version.

U8 (Go Sample Rewrite): The existing sample chaincode (likely simplekey-value) will be analyzed and rewritten to be idiomatic Go, utilizing goroutines for concurrency where appropriate, proper error handling with `fmt.Errorf`, and clear struct definitions.
assumptions: U2 and U3 are identical user stories. I will treat them as a single requirement to avoid duplicate effort.
The Kafka health checks from the 'master' branch (U4) are already implemented and tested. The effort is for merge/backport and validation, not new feature development.
I have full access to the Hyperledger Fabric codebase (Go, Node.js, Java SDKs, core fabric code) and its build/test infrastructure.
The effort estimates account for time required to write unit and integration tests for the changes.
For U5, I am assuming the necessary internal APIs for operation-level introspection in the chaincode shim are available or will be developed as part of this task.
The operations service (U7) already has a framework for serving metadata; adding a new endpoint is a well-understood extension.

activities.activity_description: Analyze all user stories (U1-U8). Review affected components, identify interdependencies, create a detailed technical plan, and set up task tracking.

For Java: Modify the chaincode shim to instantiate a new transaction context per invocation for thread-safety. For Node.js: Ensure the documentation clarifies the context is the first parameter. Write unit tests.

Physically move 'protos/utils' to a new 'protoutils' top-level package. Update all internal imports across the Fabric codebase and tooling. Update public documentation. Perform a clean build and test.
Identify the relevant commit(s) from master. Merge or cherry-pick into the release-1.4 branch. Resolve any conflicts. Run the integration test suite for ordering service with Kafka.

activities.activity_name: U5: Implement Read-Permission Invoke for Queries
activities.activity_description: Modify the transaction validation logic to inspect chaincode operations. Implement policy that allows `Get`-only transactions with Reader permission. Add a `ReadOnlyInvoke` path if operation-level inspection is too complex. Develop comprehensive tests for both permission cases.

activities.activity_name: U6: Add Service Discovery External Endpoint Config
activities.activity_description: Introduce the new peer configuration parameter. Modify the Service Discovery module to read and use this parameter when advertising peer endpoints. Write unit tests for the configuration logic and integration tests with a mock discovery service.

activities.activity_name: U7: Expose Version via Operations Service
activities.activity_description: Add a `/version` endpoint to the operations service for both peer and orderer. Implement the handler to read and return the node's version. Write unit tests for the new endpoint.

activities.activity_name: U8: Rewrite Go Sample to Idiomatic Go
activities.activity_description: Analyze existing sample chaincode. Rewrite it following Go best practices, including proper error handling, use of structs, and comments explaining Go-specific constructs. Update related documentation.
Perform peer code review for all changes. Integrate all components, run the full system test suite (including the new tests), and address any integration issues.
